title: CutAddPaste: Time Series Anomaly Detection by Exploiting Abnormal Knowledge

problem.claim: Time-series anomaly detection is difficult because anomalies are rare, sample categories are imbalanced, and anomaly labeling is costly and challenging.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often assume normality and overlook labeled abnormal samples; existing anomaly-assumption augmentation methods are random or coarse-grained, focus on pointwise anomalies, and lack cutting-edge domain knowledge.

contributions.claim: Introduces CutAddPaste, an anomaly assumption-based approach for time-series anomaly detection.
Uses prior anomaly knowledge to generate pseudo anomalies by cutting temporal patches, adding linear trends, and pasting them into other samples.
Targets both point and pattern anomalies through patch-based augmentation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CutAddPaste as a novel anomaly assumption-based approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on standard benchmark datasets are reported to show that CutAddPaste outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time-series anomaly detection is difficult because anomalies are rare, data are imbalanced, and labeling is costly.
Existing methods often rely on normality assumptions and overlook abnormal samples; existing augmentation approaches are limited in anomaly coverage and domain knowledge.
The paper introduces CutAddPaste, which generates pseudo anomalies using prior anomaly knowledge.
The method cuts temporal patches, adds linear trends, and pastes them into other samples to approximate point and pattern anomalies.
The authors report superior performance on standard benchmark datasets compared with state-of-the-art approaches.

source_observation.claim: The method combines patch cutting, linear trend addition, and pasting to generate pseudo anomalies.

interpretation.claim: Augmentation that models both local segments and temporal trends may represent a broader range of anomaly structures than pointwise perturbations.

application.claim: For time-series anomaly detection, design augmentation operators around known anomaly forms rather than relying only on random pointwise changes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which anomaly types, datasets, or conditions benefit most from the approach.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, or performance magnitudes.
The abstract does not describe the implementation, training protocol, or ablation results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
